header: THE TRAINS AT DURGAPUR RAILWAY STATION (DGR): I show the mail and express trains first, in two lists (towards Howrah, and away from it), then the local MEMU trains in both directions below them. Each train shows its time at Durgapur (the departure, large; the arrival under it), its name and number, where it starts and ends, and the days it runs (Daily, or the weekdays); a special train is marked. The next train of each list that runs today is marked and the ones already gone today are dimmed. There are two switches: only the trains that run today, and whether the special trains are shown. It is the TIMETABLE (src/lib/live/railway.ts reads RailRadar's station timetable and checks it), not live running status, and the card says so, says when it was fetched, names its source and links the official live enquiry. Nothing typed is sent anywhere: the request carries nothing, and the plant's API key never leaves the server.

symbols.name: momentNow
doc: Here I get the time and the day of the week now at Durgapur.

symbols.name: useClock
doc: The clock of the card. I keep it as the card's own small state, ticking every half minute, so that nothing else redraws the lists.

symbols.name: HEADROOM
doc: THE HEADROOM OF A TRIMMED TITLE. The trim puts the top of the box at the height of a capital, and a title that is cut with an ellipsis (overflow hidden) would shave whatever stands higher: in Poppins the tops of b, d, h, k, l (4% of the size above a capital), the dot of i and the tops of f and j (10%). So I give the box 0.12 em of room above it and the same amount of negative margin, which leaves the text exactly where it was and lets those tops show. Measured on the card: a render with the clipping on differs from one with it off in the tops of those letters; with the headroom they are the same.

doc: This draws one train. I keep the top of the time and the top of the first line on one row of pixels (the same trimming as the flights card: the room above a capital is trimmed from both, the time let down 0.05 em for Poppins' round digits). Props: `fares` is the fare button (on by default); `origin` is the station the fares start from, Durgapur unless the Asansol tab says ASN (a train that ends at that station has no fare onward); `extra` is a chip of the caller's own beside the days.

behaviours: the card names the station and its code and says how many trains it holds
it explains the two times: the departure large and the arrival under it, and that the days are the days at Durgapur
there are two sections, the express and mail trains first and the local trains below them, each in two directions
a train shows its time (the departure, 00:06 for 13135), its arrival under it (arr 00:04), name, number and class
the two ends are spelt out with the code beside the name and the city and state under: 13135 runs from Kolkata Chitpur (KOAA) to Jaynagar (JYG), Kolkata, West Bengal to Jaynagar, Bihar
every code has its full name written out, not 'Jn': Howrah Junction (HWH) → Gorakhpur Junction (GKP) style, and the station code has a hover note
a station that is not in the table keeps the name the railway source gives, with its code and no place: Newplace (ZZZZ)
a train that starts here says so and one that ends here says so
the days are chips: Daily for the daily trains, the day at Durgapur for the rest (13135 is Sun, not Sat)
a special train is marked Special
when every train is placed there is no third list; a train the data cannot place goes in a closed details block, saying why, with where it starts and ends
the next train that runs today is marked with the wait: on Wednesday at 10:00 the first marked one is a Wednesday train after 10:00
trains already gone today are dimmed, and none are dimmed at one minute past midnight
the switches are buttons that say whether they are on: only trains that run today (off) and special trains (on)
with 'only today' on, trains of other days are left out (13135 runs only on Sunday); with specials off, no Special chip
the card says plainly that it is the timetable, NOT live running status (no delay, cancellation or platform), that the railway revises timings, and links the official live enquiry
it names how the days and the direction are worked out, not as facts the source stated
its links open in a new tab with noopener, and the plant's key is nowhere in the page
the lists scroll inside the card (a station has hundreds of trains) and can be reached by keyboard
a junction is picked out in amber (tinted, ringed, with a hover note); a station that is not a junction is not
the bottom of the card writes out every short form: the class codes (EC = Executive Chair Car), MEMU, station codes, GST, IRCTC, NTES
the legend names the amber junction and the violet MEMU panel
the local (MEMU) section is violet all through: panel, MEMU badge, heading, rows and day chips; the express section has none of it
a Vande Bharat and a Shatabdi are marked by their own badge, thick edge and tint (cyan, indigo); no other train is
the legend names the premium trains
every express and mail train that goes on from Durgapur has a '₹ Fares' button, and every local (MEMU) one that goes on has a '₹ Fare hint' button; a train that ends at Durgapur has none
the fare panel is closed until the button is pressed (no request is made by a page of 250 trains)
a fare table names the end station with its code, the distance, the day asked for and each class with its rupees and parts
only the classes the train has are listed (no 2A, no 1A, no chair car here)
the fare table carries a ONE-LINE disclaimer (approximate, may differ when you book, check IRCTC): no long paragraph
a train with no fare in the reservation system says so in a short line instead of showing a number
the notes say fares are asked for with the button, and that local trains get an estimate from the published fare table, not a lookup
the date the fares were last received is said first and plainly, with how long ago: 'Fares last received from the railway: Sat 14 Nov 2026 (today)', in green when fresh
the days are counted in Indian days: 7 pm UTC on 13 Nov is 00:30 on 14 Nov in India (today); 13 Nov at 06:00 IST is yesterday; 7 Nov is 7 days ago
fares more than seven days old are called old, in amber, with their age
when the paid service has ended the card says the fares are no longer refreshed and may have changed, even for recent fares, in amber
a table with no received time (a plain set) shows no received line
a hint says 'Fare hint' and 'about Rs 10', names the end station and the distance, and shows the table slabs it came from
a range is shown as 'about Rs 35-40'
the hint's disclaimer is one short line: an estimate, not a lookup, the ticket counter's fare applies
a hint does not talk like a reservation fare: no 'Asked for travel on', no 'Unreserved (general) fares are not published', no 'Approximate.' disclaimer
a MEMU with an express number (13180) is told it may cost more, a passenger MEMU number (63505) is not
a hint is dated by the day the table was applied, in green, and is never called old or no longer refreshed even when it was made months ago or after the paid month
under a stops table the codes it uses are written out (not only on hover), with km explained
the fares to every stop: one row per stop with its name, code and kilometres from Durgapur, one column per class (cheapest first), a dash where the train does not sell the class to that stop
a junction stop is picked out in amber, an ordinary stop is not; the table scrolls inside the panel, sideways and down, keeping its header and the stop names in view (a phone, 57 stops)
the table names the date the OLDEST fare was received, with how long ago, in short words; the one-line disclaimer follows
a table of fares more than a week old, or after the paid month, is amber and says so
the stops of a local train are hints: 'Fare hints', 'about Rs 10', a range 'about Rs 35-40', the one-line estimate disclaimer, and never called old or frozen
the stops table is not opened by a page of trains (no request until the fares panel and its stops button are pressed)

a local train with no hint (it reverses) says so in one short line and points to the ticket counter; an express train with no fare says so and to check IRCTC; the two are not mixed, and neither carries the fare disclaimer

each scrolling list is positioned (relative), so the absolutely placed screen-reader words inside its rows are clipped with it and do not stretch the window's scroll area into a blank space under the card
the time and the first line start on the same row of pixels (the trimming of the flights card)

the title has headroom above it (padding and an equal negative margin) so that the tops of b, d, h, l, f and the dot of i are not shaved by the ellipsis clip that the capital-height trim would otherwise cause
the card asks the server once an hour (the server itself keeps the answer twelve hours)
'durgapur railway station trains' and its like open the card
'train fare' and its like open the card (where the fare finder is), and a flight fare does not open it
the other live cards keep their words: weather, flights, airport
a line with words that are not the card's does not open it (ticket booking, a tyre, a plain sum)
the sample questions are the card's own words
